headline: GOLD LEAPS TO $4,490 AS JULY FOMC MINUTES EXPOSE 9-3 RATE-HIKE SPLIT — DOLLAR TANKS, SEPTEMBER HIKE ODDS COLLAPSE TO ONE-IN-THREE
snippet: Gold surged more than 3.5% on Wednesday August 19 to $4,490 per ounce — its highest level since early June — as the U.S. Dollar Index sold off on a Treasury buyback plan targeting the 10-to-30-year sector, bringing long yields sharply lower. The July FOMC minutes confirmed the most divided Fed vote since September 2016: a 9-to-3 split with Hammack (Cleveland), Kashkari (Minneapolis), and Logan (Dallas) all voting for an immediate 25-bp hike over Chair Warsh's hold. Three weak data prints since July 29 — payrolls -23,000, CPI +0.1% monthly, retail sales -0.6% — have since eroded September hike odds from roughly 60% to one-in-three, a policy recalibration that is structurally bullish for gold heading into the August 28 Jackson Hole keynote.

headline: NEXGOLD GOLDBORO RC INFILL DELIVERS 5.26 g/t Au OVER 7m AND 7.08 g/t OVER 5m — 76% OF 40,000m FEASIBILITY DRILL COMPLETE IN NOVA SCOTIA
snippet: NexGold Mining Corp. (TSXV: NEXG) announced August 19 that its Reverse Circulation infill drill program at the Goldboro Gold Project in Nova Scotia has returned 5.26 g/t gold over 7.0 metres and 7.08 g/t gold over 5.0 metres from 85 RC holes representing 3,591 metres drilled within the west pit area. The 40,000-metre program is now 76% complete and is specifically designed to support a final investment decision and potential inclusion in a Mineral Resource update beyond the Feasibility Study expected later in 2026. Goldboro is one of the few advanced-stage Atlantic Canadian gold projects with a feasibility-ready drilling program actively de-risking the resource — consistent high-grade hits from an infill program that is 76% done meaningfully narrows execution risk ahead of FID.

headline: ONYX GOLD HITS 67m OF 1.7 g/t Au WITH VISIBLE GOLD AT 73.4 g/t — ARGUS MAIN DELIVERS MUNRO-CROESUS PROJECT'S BROADEST HIGH-GRADE HIT
snippet: Onyx Gold Corp. (TSXV: ONYX) reported August 19 that hole MC26-340 at the Argus Main zone of its 100%-owned Munro-Croesus Project — 75 km east of Timmins, Ontario — returned 1.7 g/t gold over 67.0 metres, including 4.1 g/t Au over 24.5 metres, 13.2 g/t Au over 6.0 metres, and a 73.4 g/t Au visible gold intersection over 1.0 metre. A companion hole drilled approximately 150 metres down-dip returned a broad interval of 0.7 g/t Au over 144.5 metres including 1.1 g/t Au over 75.0 metres. Results span the Argus Main and Argus West zones with regional MZ Zone assays still pending — making this an open-ended positive result from one of the more prolific drill programs currently running in the Timmins gold camp.

headline: KIRKLAND LAKE DISCOVERIES PUSHES MIRADO 80m DEEPER — 20.29 g/t Au STEP-OUT EXTENDS NORTH ZONE 140m BELOW HISTORIC RESOURCE, ONTARIO
snippet: Kirkland Lake Discoveries Corp. (TSXV: KLDC) released August 19 results from seven additional drill holes at the Mirado Gold Project in Ontario, highlighted by hole KLM26-022 returning 4.4 metres grading 20.29 g/t gold in the South Zone and an 80-metre step-out hole returning broad lower-grade intervals confirming a wide mineralized envelope. The North Zone was extended approximately 140 metres below the existing historical resource, while six regional holes at the MZ Zone and four holes southwest of Mirado intersected intense hydrothermal alteration and sulphide mineralization with assays pending — suggesting the Mirado system sits within a broader gold-bearing corridor that warrants continued systematic drilling.

headline: GLENCORE, ANGLO, RIO: CRITICAL MINERAL SCRUTINY NOW A PERMANENT FEATURE OF MAJOR M&A — COPPER ASSETS FACE LONGEST REVIEWS
snippet: Executives at Glencore, Anglo American, and Rio Tinto confirmed in August 19 comments to Mining Weekly that antitrust reviews and national interest tests have become significantly more prominent in major mining M&A, particularly for transactions involving copper and other critical minerals — though they characterize the increased scrutiny as a new planning variable rather than a fundamental dealbreaking constraint. The acknowledgment from three of the world's largest miners signals a structural shift: governments are treating copper, lithium, and rare earths as strategic assets whose ownership matters in ways iron ore never did. For junior investors, this matters directly — a longer, more complex approval process for acquisitions extends the holding period before major bids materialize, but it also signals that sovereign-backed buyers are willing to pay to secure supply.

headline: SILVER RETREATS TO $63.10 AS GOLD SURGES 3.5% — SHARPEST GOLD-SILVER DIVERGENCE IN WEEKS ON FOMC MINUTES DAY
snippet: Silver September futures fell to $63.10 per ounce on August 19 — down 0.38% from Tuesday's close — while gold surged more than 3.5% to $4,490 on the same session, producing one of the sharpest intraday gold-silver divergences in recent weeks. The gold-silver ratio widened sharply as Treasury's buyback plan targeting the long end of the yield curve primarily benefited gold's monetary store-of-value role over silver's industrial demand component. Silver's failure to participate in gold's FOMC-driven rally is technically notable: silver had been outperforming gold on a month-to-date basis (up 14% in August vs gold's 9%), but the divergence today raises a question about whether the industrial demand premium that drove silver above $65 last week is beginning to moderate.

headline: CHILE WEATHER EXTENDS CASERONES DISRUPTION — COPPER PHYSICAL SQUEEZE HITS WIDEST SPOT PREMIUM SINCE 2021 AS INVENTORIES FALL
snippet: Severe weather in Chile has prolonged the operational disruption at the Caserones copper mine, pushing up recovery costs and extending the restoration timeline, according to Rio Times reporting from August 18. The Caserones setback compounds an already-extreme physical market tightness: LME cash copper was trading more than $540 per tonne above the three-month contract — the widest spot premium since the 2021 short squeeze — while Comex front-month contracts held near $6.60 per pound as exchange inventories fell from 244,000 to below 215,000 tonnes in two weeks. For TSX-V copper junior investors, this structural gap between physical spot and forward prices is the clearest signal of how urgently new copper supply is needed — and that urgency directly supports the valuation multiples being assigned to high-grade copper discoveries like NAK and Cowley.

headline: LITHIUM CARBONATE HITS 5-MONTH LOW OF CNY 140,000 — AUSTRALIAN AND CHINESE MINE RESTARTS REIGNITE OVERSUPPLY FEARS
snippet: Lithium carbonate prices fell to CNY 140,000 per tonne in August 2026 — their lowest level in nearly six months — as a wave of restarted production collides with softening near-term consumption signals. Mineral Resources restarted its 165,000 dmt/year Bald Hill spodumene mine in Western Australia after an 18-month suspension, Core Lithium restarted its Finniss Project in the Northern Territory, and Chinese production remains elevated. China also ended tax exemptions for lithium-ion batteries in a move to stem margin compression among battery manufacturers — a policy change that may slow downstream investment without resolving the supply surplus. Global lithium production is projected to grow 26% year-over-year in 2026, and the supply overhang that suppressed prices through 2024 appears to be structurally reasserting itself despite robust long-run EV and grid storage demand.

headline: DOE BACKS 9 PROJECTS WITH $134M TO PULL CRITICAL MINERALS FROM U.S. MINE WASTE — RARE EARTH SUPPLY CHAIN PUSH BYPASSES PERMITTING BOTTLENECK
snippet: The U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation announced $134 million in funding for projects designed to recover rare earth elements and other critical minerals from mine waste, industrial feedstocks, and secondary sources — deliberately targeting already-disturbed sites to bypass the slow primary mine permitting process. The program reflects Washington's acknowledgment that building a domestic critical mineral supply chain on newly-permitted primary mines alone would take decades, while legacy mine sites and coal ash streams offer a faster pathway to REE feedstock for U.S. magnet and battery manufacturing. For North American rare earth investors, federal capital deployment at this scale is a direct market signal: the U.S. government treats REE supply chain buildout as a national infrastructure priority, and that framing typically precedes procurement contracts and subsidized processing capacity.
